title: Fill Lightness
---

<!-- llm-context: fill-lightness / -fill-lightness utility — adjusts SVG fill colour lightness using CSS relative colour syntax across 17 colour spaces. fill-lightness-{n} to lighten, -fill-lightness-{n} to darken, with optional /{color-space} modifier. fill-lighten-{n} and fill-darken-{n} are user-friendly aliases. -->

# Fill Lightness

Adjust the lightness of any SVG fill colour using CSS relative colour syntax. Use `fill-lightness-{amount}` to lighten and `-fill-lightness-{amount}` to darken. Works across 17 colour spaces with a simple slash modifier.

Lightness utilities are also available for [background](/guide/lightness), [text](/guide/text-lightness), [stroke](/guide/stroke-lightness), [outline](/guide/outline-lightness), and [accent](/guide/accent-lightness).

::: tip Import
Included in `@import 'tw-jib-css'`. To import individually:
```css
@import 'tw-jib-css/lightness';
```
:::

## Quick Reference

Formulas use `amt` for `var(--tw-jib--fill-lightness--amount)` — set to `<amount> × 0.01` (lighten) or `<amount> × −0.01` (darken).

<QuickReference :rows="[
  { class: 'fill-lightness-<amount>', styles: 'fill: oklch(from var(--tw-jib--fill-color) calc(l * (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) + max(0, amt)) calc(c * min(1, (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) * 5)) h / alpha)' },
  { class: '-fill-lightness-<amount>', styles: 'fill: oklch(from var(--tw-jib--fill-color) calc(l * (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) + max(0, amt)) calc(c * min(1, (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) * 5)) h / alpha)' },
  { class: 'fill-lightness-<amount>/oklch', styles: 'fill: oklch(from var(--tw-jib--fill-color) calc(l * (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) + max(0, amt)) calc(c * min(1, (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) * 5)) h / alpha)' },
  { class: 'fill-lightness-<amount>/hsl', styles: 'fill: hsl(from var(--tw-jib--fill-color) h calc(s * min(1, min(l, 100 - l) / max(min(L2, 100 - L2), 0.5))) L2 / alpha) — L2 = l * (1 - max(amt, 0 - amt)) + max(0, amt) * 100' },
  { class: 'fill-lightness-<amount>/color-mix', styles: 'fill: color-mix(in oklab, var(--tw-jib--fill-color), white calc(amt * 100%))' },
]" />

## Basic Usage

### Lighten

Set a base fill colour with `fill-{color}`, then lighten it with `fill-lightness-{amount}`:

<Example stretch>
  <div class="flex gap-4 items-center">
    <svg class="w-10 h-10 fill-blue-500" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M11.645 20.91l-.007-.003-.022-.012a15.247 15.247 0 01-.383-.218 25.18 25.18 0 01-4.244-3.17C4.688 15.36 2.25 12.174 2.25 8.25 2.25 5.322 4.714 3 7.688 3A5.5 5.5 0 0112 5.052 5.5 5.5 0 0116.313 3c2.973 0 5.437 2.322 5.437 5.25 0 3.925-2.438 7.111-4.739 9.256a25.175 25.175 0 01-4.244 3.17 15.247 15.247 0 01-.383.219l-.022.012-.007.004-.003.001a.752.752 0 01-.704 0l-.003-.001z"/></svg>

    <svg class="w-10 h-10 fill-blue-500 fill-lightness-40" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M11.645 20.91l-.007-.003-.022-.012a15.247 15.247 0 01-.383-.218 25.18 25.18 0 01-4.244-3.17C4.688 15.36 2.25 12.174 2.25 8.25 2.25 5.322 4.714 3 7.688 3A5.5 5.5 0 0112 5.052 5.5 5.5 0 0116.313 3c2.973 0 5.437 2.322 5.437 5.25 0 3.925-2.438 7.111-4.739 9.256a25.175 25.175 0 01-4.244 3.17 15.247 15.247 0 01-.383.219l-.022.012-.007.004-.003.001a.752.752 0 01-.704 0l-.003-.001z"/></svg>

### Darken

Use `-fill-lightness-{amount}` to decrease lightness:

## Colour Spaces

Use the slash modifier to select a colour space. Different spaces produce visually distinct results. For background on each colour space, see the [Colour Spaces guide](/guide/colour-spaces). For details on how scaling works, see [Background Lightness](/guide/lightness#how-scaling-works).

### Lighten across colour spaces


<Example stretch>

## Aliases

For convenience, `fill-lighten-*` and `fill-darken-*` are provided as user-friendly aliases that map to the same underlying utilities:

| Alias | Equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `fill-lighten-{amount}` | `fill-lightness-{amount}` |
| `fill-lighten-{amount}/{space}` | `fill-lightness-{amount}/{space}` |
| `fill-darken-{amount}` | `-fill-lightness-{amount}` |
| `fill-darken-{amount}/{space}` | `-fill-lightness-{amount}/{space}` |

Both forms produce identical CSS output. Use whichever reads better in your markup:

```html
<!-- These are equivalent -->
<svg class="fill-blue-500 fill-lightness-20">...</svg>
<svg class="fill-blue-500 fill-lighten-20">...</svg>

<!-- These are equivalent -->
<svg class="fill-blue-500 -fill-lightness-20">...</svg>
<svg class="fill-blue-500 fill-darken-20">...</svg>
```
